    Bilinear forms and base change #

    This file extends bilinear forms to abstract base changes through IsBaseChange.bilinForm, using Mathlib's canonical tensor base change and transport along a linear equivalence. It also records how nondegeneracy behaves under base change.

    Nondegeneracy is not preserved by an arbitrary base change: a form can acquire a kernel when its discriminant becomes a zero divisor. On a finite free module it is exactly the nonvanishing of that discriminant, so any structure map between integral domains reflects it, and an injective one also preserves it. The theorems LinearMap.BilinForm.nondegenerate_of_nondegenerate_baseChange and LinearMap.BilinForm.nondegenerate_baseChange_iff, and the computations behind them, LinearMap.BilinForm.toMatrix_baseChange and LinearMap.BilinForm.det_toMatrix_baseChange, say that base change acts entrywise on the Gram matrix of a basis and maps its determinant accordingly.

    When the scalar algebra is free over the original semiring, base change preserves left separation and nondegeneracy without any finiteness or freeness hypothesis on the module carrying the form. In particular, this applies to arbitrary extensions of fields, even in infinite dimension. Injective localizations also preserve separation and nondegeneracy without any condition on the module carrying the form.

    Over an ordered field, base change into a linearly ordered commutative ring along an order-preserving structure map also preserves and reflects positive definiteness of the quadratic map associated to a bilinear form on a finite-dimensional space; this is how a rational form is compared with its real extension.

    Main declarations #

    • IsBaseChange.bilinForm: extension to an abstract base change, characterized by its values on the original module.
    • IsBaseChange.bilinForm_tmul: extension commutes with tensor products of bilinear forms.
    • LinearMap.SeparatingLeft.baseChange: a free scalar extension preserves left separation.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.Nondegenerate.baseChange: a free scalar extension preserves nondegeneracy, without a finite-dimensionality assumption.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.Nondegenerate.baseChange_of_isLocalization: an injective localization preserves nondegeneracy, without a freeness or finiteness assumption on the module.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.liftBaseChange: lifting a form-preserving map preserves the base-changed form, without assuming the map exhibits a base change.
    • IsBaseChange.bilinForm_baseChange: if a bilinear form restricts along a map to a second form, evaluating it through the associated base-change equivalence agrees with the canonical base change of the second form.
    • IsBaseChange.bilinFormIsometryEquiv: in that situation the base-change equivalence is an isometric equivalence from the canonical base change of the second form.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.baseChange_baseChange_baseChange: base-changed maps preserving a bilinear form preserve its base change.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.toMatrix_baseChange: the Gram matrix of a base-changed form, in the base-changed basis, is the entrywise image of the original Gram matrix.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.det_toMatrix_baseChange: the determinant of that Gram matrix is the image of the original determinant.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.nondegenerate_of_nondegenerate_baseChange: a bilinear form on a finite free module over an integral domain is nondegenerate as soon as its base change into a second integral domain is, with no hypothesis on the structure map.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.nondegenerate_baseChange_iff: along an injective structure map between integral domains the implication is an equivalence.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.IsometryEquiv.baseChange: an isometric equivalence of bilinear forms base-changes to an isometric equivalence of their base changes.
    • LargeIndecomposable.Foundations.bilinFormBaseChangeProdIsometry: base change commutes with products of bilinear forms, via the canonical tensor-product equivalence.
    • LinearMap.BilinForm.posDef_toQuadraticMap_baseChange_iff: along an order-preserving structure map from an ordered field to a linearly ordered commutative ring, base change preserves and reflects positive definiteness of the quadratic map of any finite-dimensional bilinear form.

        Nondegeneracy descends along any base change of integral domains. On a finite free module, nondegeneracy of a bilinear form is nonvanishing of the determinant of its Gram matrix, and the structure map sends that determinant to the determinant of the base-changed Gram matrix, so a nondegenerate base change forces a nondegenerate form.             Positive definiteness is preserved and reflected by an ordered scalar extension. For a bilinear form on a finite-dimensional space over an ordered field F, and a linearly ordered commutative ring K whose structure map from F is strictly monotone, the quadratic map of the base change of B to K is positive definite exactly when that of B is. No symmetry assumption is needed. In particular a rational form is positive definite exactly when its real extension is.
